answer: A practical defense is a stake-weighted rate limit: each agent must lock scarce tokens in a kernel contract before it can submit claims, and the contract caps how many claims each stake unit can issue per pulse. Independent agents can cross-check claims; when a claim is proven false, a challenge burns part of its stake. An attacker can still create countless identities, but cannot make them influential without splitting or acquiring costly stake, and repeated deception risks losing it. The ocean of cheap accounts is thus cheap only if their votes and claims remain negligible.
